name: umount
description: Detaches a mounted filesystem, flushing pending writes before releasing it.

flags.description: Lazy unmount: detach now, clean up when active accesses finish.
Force unmount (mainly for dead NFS mounts).

examples.explanation: Safely detaches the filesystem. Data is flushed; the device can then be removed.
"Target is busy" means some process still uses the mount. Find it: lsof +f -- /mnt/share or fuser -vm /mnt/share, close it, retry.
Lazy unmount for stubborn cases: the mount disappears from the tree immediately; open file handles finish before cleanup.

about: umount refuses when files are open or a process has its working directory inside the mount — this is data protection, not a bug. USB devices must be unmounted (or safely ejected) before removal to avoid losing buffered writes.
mistakes: Pulling a USB drive without unmounting and losing the last seconds of writes.
Not finding the busy process — check fuser -vm or lsof.
warnings: Force-unmounting (-f) can leave the filesystem needing an fsck; use -l instead when possible.
